subject: general
question: According to the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, what was the forest cover in India as a percentage of its total geographical area in 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**21.76%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report, 2025** was released by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, Government of India.
 
• According to the report, the **forest cover** in India as a percentage of its **total geographical area** for the year **2023** was recorded as **21.76%**.
 
• This indicator is part of the monitoring mechanism for **SDG Goal 15**, which focuses on **"Life on Land"** and aims to protect, restore, and promote the sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems.
 
• The data utilized in the **NIF Progress Report** is primarily derived from the assessments conducted by the **Forest Survey of India (FSI)** and is mapped to the progress of the **United Nations' 2030 Agenda**.
 
• Maintaining and increasing the **forest cover** is essential for **biodiversity conservation**, carbon sequestration, and ensuring ecological balance in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India State of Forest Report (ISFR)**:
 
 
• The **Forest Survey of India (FSI)**, an organization under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, publishes this **biennial report**.
 
• The **ISFR 2021** assessment (the **17th cycle**) reported the total forest cover of India to be **7,13,789 sq km**.
 
• This figure represented **21.71%** of the **total geographical area** of India (**3,287,469 sq km**). The **21.76%** figure in the **2025 Progress Report** reflects the updated indicators within the **National Indicator Framework**.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Forest Cover**:
 
 
• Forest cover is classified into three categories based on canopy density: **Very Dense Forest** (density > 70%), **Moderately Dense Forest** (density 40%–70%), and **Open Forest** (density 10%–40%).
 
• Any land with a **tree canopy density** of more than **10%** and an area of more than **1 hectare** is considered forest cover, regardless of land ownership or legal status.
 
 
 
• **State-wise Data**:
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** has the largest **forest cover** in terms of **area** in the country.
 
• In terms of **percentage** of geographical area, **Mizoram** ranks highest at approximately **84.53%**, followed by **Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 15 (SDG 15)**:
 
 
• This goal targets the **sustainable management of forests**, combating **desertification**, and halting **land degradation** and **biodiversity loss**.
 
• India's **National Indicator Framework** tracks **12 indicators** specifically under SDG 15 to monitor domestic progress.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Forest Policy, 1988**: The government aims to bring **33%** of the total geographical area under **forest and tree cover** to ensure environmental stability and ecological security.
 
• **Tree Cover**: Unlike forest cover, **tree cover** refers to isolated or small patches of trees (less than **1 hectare**) found outside the recorded forest area. When combined, the **Total Forest and Tree Cover** in India is approximately **24.62%** of the total area.
 
• **Carbon Stock**: The total **carbon stock** in the country's forests is estimated to be around **7,204 million tonnes**, showing an increase compared to previous assessments, which is a key metric for **climate change mitigation**.
 
• **NIF Progress Report 2025**: This report serves as a critical document for **policymakers** to understand the gap between current achievements and the **2030 targets** set by the **United Nations**.
</ul
